newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican corn imports could fall 53 pct in 97 vs 96.
newsitem.headline: Mexican corn imports could fall 53 pct in 97 vs 96.

text.p: Greater corn production in Mexico in 1997 could help ease corn imports by up to 53 percent to 2.8 million tonnes, compared with 5.9 million tonnes in 1996, an official from the Naitonal Chamber of Industrial Corn Chamber said on Wednesday.
"Corn imports will not be more than 2.8 million tonnes at most, compared with 5.9 million in 1996," a chamber director who declined to be named told Reuters.
He said that a crop of more than two million tonnes being harvested in Sinaloa state is the greatest quantity seen there in the past four or five years.
A greater national supply should reduce corn importlevels seen in recent years, he said.
The chamber expects a crop of more than 17 million tonnes.
In the first four months of the year Mexico's grain purchases from the exterior cost $85.9 million, compared with import costs of $368.5 million in the same period in 1996.
